historicalReferences: Think back to 1979, the year of the infamous fight between the brothers, a Daytona moment that still resonates today.
Richard Petty's record seven Daytona 500 wins remain a benchmark of excellence on this iconic oval.
The 1976 finish, where David Pearson limped across the line after a last-lap crash, is etched in Daytona lore.
Cale Yarborough and Donnie Allison's last-lap crash in '79 allowed Richard Petty to win. A legendary finish.
Jeff Gordon's emotional final win at Daytona in 2015 was a fitting end to a Hall of Fame career.
The Earnhardt legacy is forever intertwined with Daytona. Dale Senior's 1998 victory remains one of the most celebrated moments in NASCAR history.
The closest finish in Daytona 500 history was in 1993, when Dale Jarrett beat Dale Earnhardt by inches.
So many careers have been defined, or destroyed, at Daytona. The stakes are always sky-high here.
The 24 Hours of Daytona is a testament to the endurance of both man and machine on this challenging circuit.
The sheer speed of the cars around this oval is breathtaking. A true test of nerve and skill.

strategyPoints: Tire wear will be a major factor on this 4.023km oval. Managing the rubber will be key to a successful race.
The pit window is relatively short here at Daytona. A quick stop is essential to avoid losing track position.
Fuel strategy will play a crucial role. Conserving fuel without sacrificing pace will be a delicate balancing act.
With the draft being so powerful, track position isn't everything. It's all about being in the right place at the right time.
Long green flag runs can really stretch the fuel mileage, forcing some teams to gamble on strategy.
The timing of caution periods can completely change the complexion of the race. Being ready to react is vital.
Aerodynamic efficiency is paramount around this oval. Minimizing drag is crucial for top speed.
The draft is everything here. Finding a good tow can make all the difference in lap time.
